issues.body: `guard_prefix` lowers `current` for every lower-indented non-opener. For a valid multiline suite such as `if (` / `    condition` / `):` / `    GATE`, the backward walk sees `):` at indentation 0, lowers `current` to 0, and then skips the real `if (` opener because its indentation is equal rather than lower. Thus the body copy derives `()` even though `_PY_OPENER` recognizes `if (`. The self-test independently asserts that `for _why, _wl_broken in (` is an opener and `):` is not, but it never passes a complete multiline header plus body through `guard_prefix`. If every copy in a cell is narrowed with the same multiline guard, all signatures can remain exactly as before, yielding a false green from this hard trust-plane gate.
issues.fix_hint:
Parse multiline Python headers as one structural header (preferably with Python token/AST positions), or make the walk preserve the opener across its closing header line without re-admitting closed sibling blocks. Add a red derivation test for `if (
    condition
):
    GATE` that requires the real enclosing guard, plus a census mutant showing a complete-cell multiline narrowing changes the cell signature and an incomplete one reds. Include a closed multiline sibling before an unguarded copy to prove the repair does not create a false enclosure.
issues.title: Multiline Python block headers make their governed body appear unguarded

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Round 3 fixes the prior arbitrary-lower-indented-statement finding, but the new syntax-filtered walk remains unsound for multiline Python block headers. The classifier recognizes the opening `if (` / `for ... in (` line, yet `guard_prefix` encounters the later dedented `):` first, lowers `current` to that header indentation, and therefore cannot admit the actual opener at the same indentation. A governed copy in that suite derives an empty guard. Applying the same multiline narrowing to all copies in a cell can consequently leave their signatures unchanged, so the hard census can green while observing none of the narrowing it claims to compare. The self-test checks classification of the two physical lines separately but never checks their combined enclosure. Because this is a new major soundness defect after the prior issue was corrected, progress is regressing under the required scale.
